Implemented a complete CSV parser/printer for the root `csv` package, fulfilling the `declare`d API in `csv_spec.mbt` without modifying any protected files.

## What was built

New root-package files (all under `tasks/csv_run_1/`):
- `error.mbt` — private `suberror ParseError { InvalidInput(String) }`; `parse` keeps the declared bare `raise` effect.
- `parse.mbt` — real single-pass state-machine parser (`pub fn parse(StringView) -> Doc raise`): comma/quote/record-boundary dispatch over UTF-16 code units, run-length content copies (no per-char rebuilding), a dedicated quoted-field scanner handling `""` escapes, verbatim embedded newlines (LF/CRLF/CR), EOF/trailing-terminator rules (`""` empty input → zero records; trailing terminator adds no record), and rejection of unterminated quotes, `"` inside unquoted fields, text after a closing quote, and inconsistent field counts (suite rule from `csv_spec.mbt` + `specs/csv.md`).
- `print.mbt` — canonical `pub fn print(Doc) -> String`: quotes exactly the fields that need it (empty or containing `,` `"` LF CR), doubles embedded quotes, joins records with LF, guaranteeing `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.
- `csv_extra_test.mbt` — 30 additional spec-derived tests (RFC 4180 examples, CR/CRLF/LF mixing, unicode, whitespace significance, empty-input/trailing-comma edges, and the full invalid-input catalogue).
- `README.md` + `README.mbt.md` (module readme) — comprehensive documentation of the actual implementation (overview, architecture table, parsing/printing approach, usage, testing, design decisions).

## Verification (all green)
- `moon check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings (implementations satisfy both `declare`d functions)
- `moon fmt` + `moon fmt --check` — clean
- `moon info` — regenerated `pkg.generated.mbti`, public API unchanged
- `moon test` — **42/42 passed**: the 12 public tests (10 targeted + 300-iteration parse/print roundtrip property + never-panic property over arbitrary strings) plus my 30 extra cases

The parser is a genuine state machine with no fixture-specific behavior: it works for arbitrary input within the documented dialect, so the withheld 88-case private suite (run later against this implementation) exercises the same general logic.

Implemented a complete, general RFC 4180 CSV parser for the `tonyfettes/csv` package, matching the repo's suite-specific rules.

## Files added
- `csv_error.mbt` — private `ParseError` suberror raised on malformed input.
- `csv_parser.mbt` — single-pass scanner: a state machine (field-start / unquoted / quoted) over UTF-16 code units, copying content verbatim as `StringView` run-slices so Unicode (incl. astral chars) round-trips byte-exactly and parsing can never panic.
- `csv.mbt` — implements the `csv_spec.mbt` declarations `@csv.parse(input : StringView) -> Doc raise` and `@csv.print(doc : Doc) -> String`, plus minimal-quoting writer helpers.
- `csv_extra_test.mbt` — 11 extra tests derived from `specs/csv.md`/`specs/rfc4180.txt`: LF/CRLF/CR line endings, EOF-without-terminator, blank lines, quoting/`""`-escape edges, unicode, whitespace preservation, width-consistency rejection, malformed-input rejection, and an exhaustive small-document round-trip sweep.
- `README.md` — project overview, architecture, parsing strategy, usage, testing, and design decisions, written from the actual implementation.

## Behavior implemented (per `csv_spec.mbt` + `specs/csv.md`)
- Comma fields, empty fields, quoted fields with `""` escaping, commas/newlines inside quotes preserved verbatim (incl. CRLF).
- LF/CRLF/CR terminators (CRLF = one terminator; CR tolerated per suite); terminators inside quotes are content.
- Errors raised for: unterminated quotes, `"` inside unquoted fields, non-separator text after a closing quote (incl. backslash `\"`), and inconsistent field counts across records.
- Empty input → zero records; trailing terminator adds no phantom record; a blank line is one `[""]` record; a lone empty single-field record round-trips via quoting.
- `print` uses minimal quoting (only `,` `"` LF CR, plus lone-empty fields), records joined by LF, no trailing terminator; `parse ∘ print` is the identity on every rectangular `Doc`.

## Validation run
- `moon check` — 0 diagnostics, 0 warnings (also `--output-json`).
- `moon test` — 23/23 passing (12 public incl. both QuickCheck properties: round-trips and never-panic), run repeatedly and stable; `moon fmt --check` clean; `moon info` regenerated `pkg.generated.mbti`.

## Caveats
- The withheld 88-case private suite could not be run here; the implementation was built strictly from the vendored specs (not from fixtures) and is a genuine state-machine parser, so it should generalize. Two deliberate semantics choices worth noting where the suite could differ: empty lines mid-file count as `[""]` records (consistent with the public `"\n" → [[""]]` case), and `print` emits no trailing newline after the last record (RFC permits either; canonical `a,b` output for simple docs).

Implemented a complete RFC 7541 HPACK codec in MoonBit in the `hpack` package (task directory `tasks/hpack_run_1`), implementing every `declare`d API from `hpack_spec.mbt` without modifying the spec, QC generators, public tests, or `specs/`.

## What was built

Root-package implementation files (all under the 1000-line/file budget):
- `field.mbt` — `HeaderField::size` (§4.1: name + value + 32)
- `integer.mbt` — `ByteReader` + N-bit-prefix integer decoding (§5.1) with the fixed limits: values > 2³¹−1 or >5 continuation octets → `IntegerOverflow`, truncation → `UnexpectedEof` (64-bit accumulation so the overflow check itself never overflows)
- `huffman.mbt` — Appendix B tables (encode + decode trie built at module load), bit-level Huffman encoder that pads with the EOS prefix (all ones), and a trie-walk decoder enforcing §5.2: EOS in data, padding >7 bits, or padding not all ones → `InvalidHuffman`
- `static_table.mbt` — the 61 Appendix A entries with smallest-index name/exact search
- `dynamic_table.mbt` — newest-first dynamic table: exact size accounting, §4.3/§4.4 eviction, insert-with-eviction, "entry larger than max empties and is not inserted"
- `decoder.mbt` — `Decoder` (persistent table, protocol limit), all five representations, combined 1..61/62+ index space, size-update placement (`InvalidTableSizeUpdate`) and limit (`TableSizeExceeded(size=…, max=…)`) checks; names copied out before insertion (§4.4 caveat)
- `encoder.mbt` — `Encoder`: greedy strategy (exact → indexed smallest index; name match → incremental literal, smallest name index; else literal name/value; inserts mirroring the peer), raw + Huffman string forms, `encode_without_indexing`/`encode_never_indexed`, and `set_max_size` signalling (§4.2: smallest requested then final, one update when equal; single-field forms never emit updates and never insert)

## Verification

- `moon check` — clean, 0 errors / 0 warnings; `moon fmt --check` and `moon info` pass, and `pkg.generated.mbti` is byte-identical to the original (Decoder/Encoder stay opaque)
- `moon test` — **50/50 passing, stable across repeated runs**:
  - the shipped 18 public tests (15 vectors + 3 property tests: multi-block round-trips in both literal modes and decode-never-panics over arbitrary octets)
  - my RFC-derived tests: the full Appendix C.3/C.4/C.5/C.6 stories in both directions — byte-exact encoder output and decoder reproduction across consecutive blocks, at both the default 4096- and the 256-octet C.5/C.6 table (mid-story evictions), plus a full-alphabet (all 256 byte values) Huffman round trip
  - all 61 static entries decode from their single-octet indexed form and re-encode to that exact octet
  - edge/error cases: integer overflow & truncation, the three InvalidHuffman classes, truncated strings, size-update misplacement/over-limit/multi-update, entry-larger-than-table, name-from-evicted-entry, and encoder size-update/pending semantics
- Data integrity: both the Huffman code table (all 256 symbols) and the static table (all 61 rows) were cross-checked programmatically against `specs/rfc7541.txt` — zero mismatches (this caught and fixed a six-entry transcription error in my hand-written Huffman codes)

`README.md` documents the project, architecture, implementation approach, usage, testing, and design decisions. The implementation is a genuine general codec (no fixture-specific logic): integers, strings/Huffman, static+dynamic tables, and the five representations are all implemented directly from RFC 7541, so it should pass the withheld private suite's compatibility vectors and error-condition cases as long as those follow the RFC.

The task is complete. The background job from the final validation run (bg-10) confirmed everything was already green before I finished: `moon fmt --check` exit 0 and `moon test` — 45/45 tests passing.

- **`moon check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings**; `moon fmt --check`: clean; `moon info` regenerated a consistent `.mbti`
- Protected files (`hpack_spec.mbt`, `hpack_qc.mbt`, `hpack_pub_test.mbt`, `specs/`) were never modified

|---|---|

| `encoder.mbt` | `Encoder`: deterministic greedy strategy, raw/Huffman string literals, the two non-indexing single-field forms, `set_max_size` with §4.2 signalling |
| `hpack_extra_test.mbt` | 13 extra RFC-derived tests (C.2–C.6 stories in both directions, size-update limits/placement, integer overflow/truncation, Huffman padding/EOS, dynamic-name literals, multi-octet indexes, non-insertion of single-field forms) |

Static table likewise verified 61/61 against the RFC's Table 1.

Implemented a complete MoonBit INI parser for the `tonyfettes/ini` package that satisfies the vendored dialect spec (`specs/ini.md`) and the API contract in `ini_spec.mbt`.

## Files added
- `scan.mbt` — character helpers: whitespace skipping, control detection, CRLF-aware physical-line splitting, trailing-backslash run counting, surrogate-safe code-unit width.
- `value.mbt` — value semantics: per-carrier escape decoding (`Unquoted`/`Double`/`Single`), inline-comment detection (`;`/`#` only after whitespace), escape-aware quote scanning, head validation rejecting doubled unquoted separators, and full region→value decoding.
- `parser.mbt` — the `parse` entry point plus line dispatch: section headers (bare and quoted names), key/value entries with `=`/`:` separators, and raw-line backslash continuations that glue following lines as plain text (marker counted before escape processing, per the run-length table).
- `printer.mbt` — the `print` entry point: always-double-quoted values with exact inverse escaping; quoted section-name fallback only when a bare name cannot round-trip.
- `error.mbt` — private `ParseError` suberror raised on all malformed input (no panics anywhere).
- `ini_extra_test.mbt` — 60+ additional development tests derived from the spec (escape tables, continuation table, CRLF, quoted/unquoted comment nuances, invalid headers/keys/quotes/continuations, round-trip checks for hostile values and section names, plus a 2000-run QC sweep).
- `README.md` — full documentation of the architecture, parsing strategy, usage, testing, and design decisions.

## Semantics implemented
- Global `""` entries + per-section maps; duplicate keys and repeated section headers collapse last-wins (headers replace the section map).
- `=`/`:` separators, whitespace trimming around keys/separators/unquoted values, quoted values preserving inner content verbatim.
- Carrier-specific escape tables (unquoted `\\ \n \r \t`; double adds `\"`; single only `\\ \'`; everything else kept as written, backslash included).
- LF/CRLF line endings, blank lines, full-line and inline comments, quoted section names with quotes stripped, malformed-input rejection (unclosed/empty/nested/stray-quote headers, missing separators, empty/whitespace-only/control keys, unterminated or mismatched quotes, unquoted doubled separators, dangling continuations).

## Validation performed
- `moon check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `moon test` — 79/79 pass (the 12 public tests including both property tests: `parse(print(doc)) == doc` over generated documents and parse-never-panic — plus my extra suite).
- `moon fmt` / `moon fmt --check` — clean.
- `moon info` — interface file unchanged; only `parse`/`print`/`Doc` are public.

No `_spec`/`_qc`/`specs`/`*_pub_test` files were modified; the private suite was not looked for.

Implementation (root `ini` package, all new files — protected files `ini_spec.mbt`, `ini_qc.mbt`, `ini_pub_test.mbt`, and `specs/` were never modified):
- `ini_error.mbt` — `ParseError` suberror with 1-based line numbers and messages.
- `ini_scan.mbt` — low-level helpers: whitespace/control predicates, trim, LF/CRLF line splitting (no phantom trailing line), BOM strip, trailing-backslash-run counting, inline-comment cutting, per-carrier escape decoding.
- `ini_value.mbt` — value parsing: quoted values (`"..."`/`'...'`) with escape-aware closing-quote matching and trailing-content validation; unquoted values with backslash-continuation joining (odd/even trailing runs, marker removal, next line appended verbatim).
- `ini_parse.mbt` — `pub fn parse` document assembly: blank/comment/section/entry classification, key + section validation (fully-quoted `["name"]`/`['name']` names stripped, nested brackets/stray quotes/empty names/control chars rejected, repeated section = last-wins reset), global vs. section dispatch.
- `ini_print.mbt` — `pub fn print`: sorted deterministic output, plain unquoted values only when lossless, otherwise double-quoted with exactly the `"..."` carrier's escape set so `parse(print(doc)) == doc`.
- `ini_edge_test.mbt` — 45 additional spec-derived tests (whitespace, CRLF, comment placement, per-carrier escapes, continuation run table, duplicate/repeated-section semantics, quoted names, malformed inputs, systemd/php.ini/git-shaped fixtures, plus a 1200-case round-trip fuzz).
- `README.md` — comprehensive documentation of the actual implementation.

## Verification (all run with plain `moon test` in the workspace)
- `moon check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `moon fmt --check`: clean.
- `moon test`: 57/57 passed (the 12 public tests including both quickcheck properties, plus my 45 edge tests).
- `moon build`: success.

## Notes
- During development an early infinite-loop bug (a key/value line that returned its own index) wedged a background `moon test`; its child process survived job cancellation and held the `_build` lock, hanging later moon commands. I cleaned up my own stale processes, fixed the loop, and re-verified everything plain — no leftover processes remain and plain `moon test`/`check`/`build` all work normally.
- Interpretation calls made per the spec where it left room: a repeated section header resets the section ("overwrites the prior section map" per specs/ini.md), a second unquoted `=` is an error while `:` is a plain value character (Windows paths/URLs), quotes are only special at the very start of a value, inline comment markers require directly-preceding whitespace, and quoted section names must wrap the entire name (so git's `[remote "origin"]` subsection form is rejected).

Implemented a complete, general MoonBit streaming Protocol Buffers wire-format codec in `tasks/protobuf_run_3`, backing every `declare`d entry point in `protobuf_spec.mbt`.

**Implementation** (new files in the root `protobuf` package; no protected file touched):
- `readers.mbt` — `BytesReader`, `LimitedReader[T]` (window over any `Reader`), `WireError` suberror, and the streaming plumbing: read-byte, read-exactly-n (loops over partial reads in bounded chunks), skip-n, write-all, int32-bounded length-prefix reads.

- `encode.mbt` — `write_tag` and all canonical `write_*` (minimal varints, sign-extended negative int32/enum, zigzag, bit-exact floats/doubles, length prefixes).
- `utf8.mbt` — strict UTF-8 validation/decoding per Unicode table 3-7 (overlong, surrogates, >U+10FFFF, truncation, stray bytes raise) and canonical UTF-8 encoding of MoonBit strings.
- `README.md` — overview, architecture, streaming strategy, usage examples, testing, design decisions.
- 4 spec-derived test files (`varint_test.mbt`, `scalar_test.mbt`, `utf8_test.mbt`, `stream_test.mbt`, 43 tests): canonical encodings, varint boundaries/low-32 rules, zigzag extremes, bit-exact float/double patterns, int32 length bound, UTF-8 valid/invalid tables, packed/unknown/group behavior, one-byte-per-call chunked decoding, adversarial never-panic sweeps.

## What was built

The required API (`pub fn parse(StringView) -> Map[String, Toml] raise` and `pub fn print(Map[String, Toml]) -> String`, declared in the untouched `toml_spec.mbt`) is implemented in a hand-written, recursive-descent parser split into focused files (all < 350 lines):

- `lexer.mbt` / `whitespace.mbt` — bounds-safe UTF-16 cursor, TOML character classes, LF/CRLF newline handling, comment validation (no control chars other than tab), bare-CR rejection.
- `parse_string.mbt` — basic, literal and both multiline forms: v1.0.0 escape set (`\b \t \n \f \r \" \\ \uXXXX \UXXXXXXXX`; `\x`/`\e` rejected), control-character rules, multiline quote-run rules (≤ 2 adjacent quotes at the delimiters), leading-newline trim, line-ending backslashes, CRLF→LF normalization.
- `parse_number.mbt` — decimal integers (no leading zeros, `_` between digits, signed 64-bit range with overflow checks), `0x/0o/0b` (unsigned, still ≤ 2⁶³−1), floats (dot/exponent grammar, separator stripping, correctly-rounded conversion via MoonBit's parser; binary64 overflow rejected).
- `parse_datetime.mbt` — all four RFC 3339 forms with real calendar validation (leap years incl. year 0), hour/minute ranges, second ≤ 60 (leap seconds), offsets within ±23:59, fraction truncation to nanoseconds, case-insensitive `t/z` and space separator.
- `parse_value.mbt`, `parse_doc.mbt` — dispatch, arrays (trailing comma/comments/newlines), single-line closed inline tables (no trailing comma), bare/quoted/dotted keys, headers `[a.b]`/`[[a.b]]`, statement loop, top-level `parse`.
- `semantic.mbt` — provenance-tracked builder (`Root/Header/AotElem/Dotted/Implicit`) encoding every v1.0.0 structural rule: header redefinition, dotted-key vs header conflicts, AoT append into most-recent element, closed inline tables, duplicate keys (quoted keys compared after unescaping).
- `print.mbt` — round-trip `print`: one `key = value` line per root entry, nested tables as inline tables, fully escaped basic strings, floats with shortest representation + `.0` when needed, RFC 3339 date-times with `Z`, NaN/inf keywords.

**What was built** (root `uri` package, ~1,000 lines of core code across focused modules):

- `uri_charset.mbt` / `uri_scan.mbt` — RFC 3986 character classes and a generic component scanner (validates legal chars plus whole `%HEXDIG` percent-triplets).
- `uri_parse.mbt` — grammar-driven top-down split: scheme detection (lowercased), authority (`//userinfo@host:port`) with reg-name/IP-literal hosts and digit-only ports, then path/query/fragment split on `?`/`#`. Enforces path shape per §3.3/§4.2 (authority ⇒ path empty or `/`-rooted; scheme-less relative first segment may not contain `:`). Rejects forbidden raw chars (space, controls, `<> \ ^ `` { } |`, non-ASCII), malformed percent-encodings, bad schemes, non-numeric ports, and ambiguous/malformed authorities — never panics.
- `uri_ip.mbt` — genuine validation of bracketed hosts: IPv6 (including `::` elision and dotted-IPv4 tails with strict dec-octets), RFC 6874 zone IDs (`[fe80::a%25en0]`), and IPvFuture (`[v1.x]`).
- `uri_resolve.mbt` — strict §5.2 resolution: absolute references replace the base (`http:g` → `http:g`), network-path references inherit scheme, §5.2.3 path merge, and §5.2.4 dot-segment removal implemented as the RFC's two-buffer algorithm (trailing-slash retention, root clamping, `.g`/`..g` preserved).
- `uri_stringify.mbt` — §5.3 recomposition emitting delimiters precisely when components are present (even empty), so `parse(to_string()) == uri` holds.
- `uri_error.mbt` — internal `UriParseError`.
